text:
lee: Heads-up — seeing a bunch of GPU pods stuck in Pending in eu-west-1. First glance looks like taint/toleration mismatch + nodeAffinity quirks. anyone else?

maria: yep saw that. pods from the new model-serving chart went into Pending about 15m ago.

sahil: can you paste the describe? most likely the helm chart override dropped the toleration.

lee: paste from one of the pods: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   2m    default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 10 node(s) had taint {gpu.pool=isolated:NoSchedule}, that the pod didn't tolerate.
```

maria: yeah the node pool template for the isolated-GPU pool has taint `gpu.pool=isolated:NoSchedule` so pods need a toleration and usually nodeAffinity `pool=gpu-isolated`.

tom: FYI autoscaler tried to spin up nodes earlier but they stayed NotReady for a bit because the warmup hook wasn't applied to the ASG launch template — that explains some scale-up lag. autoscaler-bot should have posted.

autoscaler-bot: [info] cluster-autoscaler: Scale-up triggered for nodegroup/gpu-isolated-eu-west-1 (1 -> 3) — 2 nodes provisioning. Estimated 120s until ready.

lee: problem is our model-serving helm values.yaml had `tolerations: []` in the top-level override (we defaulted to empty to 'simplify'), so the main container isn't tolerating `gpu.pool`. The sidecar chart does include tolerations though (which is why logs looked ok). :facepalm:

sahil: quick patch option: add toleration to the deployment without doing a chart bump: 
```
kubectl patch deployment model-server -n ml --type='json' -p='[ { "op": "add", "path": "/spec/template/spec/tolerations", "value": [{ "key": "gpu.pool", "operator": "Equal", "value": "isolated", "effect": "NoSchedule" }] } ]'
```

maria: also double-check nodeAffinity. our pods have `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` with `matchExpressions: {key: pool, operator: In, values: [gpu-isolated]}` — but some old nodes were labeled `pool=gpu` (missing -isolated) so scheduler doesn't match even if toleration is present. We should standardize labels on nodepool templates.

tom: ops note: ASG/launch-template fix I rolled ensures new nodes come up with label `pool=gpu-isolated` and taint applied. Old nodegroups might need `kubectl label node <node> pool=gpu-isolated` + drain/replace.

ops-bot: quick reminder: draining nodes with GPUs will evict pods unsafely unless `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` is used and you accept eviction delays. Use the `--force` checklist in the runbook.

lee: can we also add a small tolerationSeconds window for preemptible workloads? curious if that helps with transient scale-down events.

sahil: tolerationSeconds only works with taint effect `NoExecute` — we use `NoSchedule` for isolation, so not applicable. Another option is to switch to `NoExecute` for short-lived preemptible pools, but that changes eviction semantics for longer running pods. Needs careful testing.

maria: action items: 1) lee apply patch to fix model-server tolerations (done?), 2) tom finish launch-template label/taint roll, 3) infra to audit nodegroup labels and add a validation in the nodepool provisioning job. I'll open a PR for the chart values to ensure tolerations are explicit.

lee: patched the deployment now — new pods are Pending but autoscaler-bot shows nodes are Ready in 50s. Will monitor. :eyes:

autoscaler-bot: [info] Added 2 nodes to nodegroup/gpu-isolated-eu-west-1. New nodes: ip-10-0-5-21, ip-10-0-6-33.

lee: pods transitioned to Running. marking this resolved for now. We'll follow up with chart and nodepool template fixes.

maria: +1. Can someone create a short postmortem note in #incidents if we hit this again? Prefer to have a one-liner cause + fix for on-call.

lee: will do if it recurs. thanks all.
